root.name: King's Indian Attack: Wahls Defense
root.moves: 1. Nf3 Nf6 2. g3 g6 3. Bg2 Bg7 4. O-O O-O 5. d3 d5

overview: Black mirrors White with a King's Indian set-up (...g6, ...Bg7, ...O-O) and also plays ...d5, a reversed Réti or KID structure. The game is slow and manoeuvring: White plays e4 and Nbd2, Black plays ...c5 and ...Nc6 with queenside play. There is little forcing theory.

white_ideas.idea: Play e4 supported by d3 and Nbd2, then expand in the centre
Prepare Re1, e5 and a kingside space grab
Keep the structure compact and wait

black_ideas.idea: Mirror the fianchetto and challenge with ...c5, ...Nc6 and ...e5

typical_structures.structure: Symmetrical fianchetto structure with pawns on d3/d5
Flexible centre where e4 or e5 may be played

character.notes: Steady manoeuvring with few forcing lines, hard to break down for either side.

structure.notes: Centre undecided; pawns on d3 and d5 with e4/e5 still to come, flexible.

approach.notes: A set-up that Black can play against many White set-ups and that mirrors the KIA.

level.notes: Plans are clear, but timing the pawn breaks needs experience.

character.reason: Slow, compact set-ups for both sides.

approach.reason: A set-up played regardless of White's reply.

plans.reason: Both sides fianchetto with a symmetrical structure.
